title: Air-fryer chicken katsu
subtitle: Japanese-style panko-crumbed chicken with tonkatsu sauce.
excerpt: Chicken breast coated in panko breadcrumbs and air-fried until golden and crisp, served with a sweet-savoury tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage. Lighter than the deep-fried original and just as satisfying. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Chicken katsu (katsu kare) became widely popular in the United Kingdom through Japanese restaurant chains in the 2010s. The dish is based on the Japanese tonkatsu preparation of breaded pork cutlet. This air-fryer version produces a comparable panko crust without deep-frying.

content.text: Chicken katsu is a breaded chicken cutlet served with a thick, dark dipping sauce made from Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, and a little ketchup. The air fryer gives you a panko crust with good colour without the splatter of deep-frying. Flatten the chicken to an even 1.5 cm so it cooks through before the crust burns.

items.prepNote: about 200 g each, pounded to 1.5 cm

content.text: Mix {{ketchup}} of ketchup with {{soy-sauce-dark}} of dark soy sauce and {{honey}} of honey. Set aside ,  this is the dipping sauce.

Set up three bowls: {{plain-flour}} of seasoned flour, {{eggs}} beaten egg, and {{breadcrumbs-panko}} of panko. Coat each {{chicken-breast}} chicken breast through flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly. Spray all over with cooking oil. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Cook for 9 minutes, flip carefully, spray again, and cook for 7-9 more minutes until golden. Rest for 3 minutes before slicing.

items.fix: Spray generously before cooking and again when you flip. Panko browns poorly without oil.

items.cause: Moved too early, or flour stage skipped.
items.fix: Wait until the first side is properly golden before flipping. Use tongs or a fish slice rather than a fork.

items.cause: Breast not pounded flat, so edges overcooked before centre done.
items.fix: Pound to a uniform 1.5 cm thickness. A thin even breast cooks much more reliably than a thick uneven one.

content.text: Chicken katsu became a British lunch staple. Serve sliced over steamed rice with shredded white cabbage and the tonkatsu sauce on the side. The same preparation works on pork loin escalopes for the classic tonkatsu version.
